neighbours.label: a function word in civic context just before a word for one's nation or state ('across the', 'of this', 'into our' + country/nation): the slot where the country is expected
fire: Thousands of teachers marched in towns and cities across the nation last spring.
Judges in this country have long upheld that principle of law.
Smugglers keep trying to sneak weapons over the border into our country.
The governor hoped that schools across the state would adopt the plan.
No citizen of this nation should be denied the right to vote.
Patriots fought to defend the freedom of our great republic.
The bill would apply to every farmer across the country.
The founders wanted the militia of a neighboring state to help.
quiet: Thousands of teachers marched down the avenue and over the bridge last spring.
The judge asked the clerk to read this motion aloud to the court.
Smugglers tried to carry the weapons up the stairs into our warehouse.
The governor walked across the room to shake hands with the mayor.
The senator signed this letter and mailed it to the voter.
Citizens filled out our survey about parking near city hall.
The bill would apply to every farmer with a license for a tractor.
The mayor wanted the budget of a local library to grow.

notes: Fires on the token before the noun; the output promotes ' nation', ' republic', ' Union'. The same words in a local setting ('across the street', 'this book') stay near zero in probes.
